sub_graphs.description: Models the security improvement from increased EXP gas costs

ambiguities.text: Benchmarks suggest EXP is 'underpriced by a factor of about 4-8' - the exact benchmark methodology and conditions are not specified.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume benchmarks were performed on typical Ethereum client implementations measuring wall-clock time for EXP operations vs gas paid. The 5x increase targets the middle of the 4-8x range.

ambiguities.text: The specification does not define how 'bytes in the exponent' is calculated for values with leading zeros.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume byte length is the minimal number of bytes needed to represent the exponent (no leading zeros counted). An exponent of 0 has 0 bytes.

implicit_assumptions.description: The 5x gas increase correctly prices the actual computational cost of exponentiation across all client implementations.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If some clients have slower EXP implementations, they could still be disproportionately affected by EXP-heavy transactions.

implicit_assumptions.description: Existing smart contracts that budget gas for EXP operations will have sufficient gas limits after the repricing.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Contracts with tight gas budgets for EXP may start failing unexpectedly, potentially locking funds or breaking protocols.

implicit_assumptions.description: Attackers cannot find other underpriced opcodes to exploit for DoS attacks.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Fixing EXP may just shift DoS attacks to other underpriced operations.
